title: host-set-override, host-unset-override, and host-set-vault should call host-audit
description:
## Background

When developers use `host-set-override`, `host-unset-override`, or `host-set-vault` to modify host settings, these changes are persisted to the system but the audit log is not automatically updated. This can cause settings changes to drift out-of-sync with audit records, making it difficult to track when and how host settings changed over time.

## Technical Approach

Add calls to `host-audit` at the end of each of these three commands:
- `host-set-override`: After successfully writing the override file
- `host-unset-override`: After successfully removing the override file
- `host-set-vault`: After successfully writing the vault.yaml file

This ensures that each settings modification is immediately reflected in the audit log. The `host-audit` command should be called with the same host as the settings modification command.

## Success Criteria

- When `host-set-override` completes, a corresponding audit entry is created
- When `host-unset-override` completes, a corresponding audit entry is created
- When `host-set-vault` completes, a corresponding audit entry is created
- Audit entries are recorded with accurate timestamps
- The feature works correctly across both Linux and macOS platforms

## Test Plan

1. Unit tests: Verify that each command calls `host-audit` with the correct host parameter
2. Integration tests: Run each command end-to-end and verify audit log entries are created
3. Platform coverage: Test on both Linux and macOS to ensure host-audit works correctly on both
4. Edge cases:
   - Verify audit is called even if settings modification fails (or document if it shouldn't be)
   - Verify behavior when host-audit command is not available

## Considerations

- The `host-audit` command may add latency to these operations — verify impact is acceptable
- Error handling: Decide whether a failed `host-audit` call should cause the entire operation to fail or just log a warning
- These three commands are frequently used — ensure the change is backward compatible and doesn't break existing workflows
close_reason: Implemented auto-audit after host-set-override, host-unset-override, and host-set-vault via _maybe_auto_audit helper in commands/_auto_audit.py. Each command passes no_audit flag through; --no-audit CLI option skips the automatic audit. Tests cover skip, success, and error-swallowing cases.

title: Monitor misses hosts when gather scans multiple hosts in same second

title: Gather performance improvement metrics for SQLite migration
description: Gather or estimate performance improvements from SQLite migration. Compare JSONL vs SQLite for: read latency (single record, bulk queries), write latency, startup time (loading data), and memory usage. Document methodology and results in docs/ or bead close reason.
close_reason:
Implemented comprehensive performance benchmarks comparing JSONL vs SQLite storage approaches. Created tools/bench_sqlite_vs_jsonl.py with both synthetic data generation and --real flag for testing against actual production files. Documented results in docs/sqlite-migration-benchmarks.md.

Key findings from real-world testing against actual ~/.fleetroll/*.jsonl files:
- Current production (32K records, 30MB): SQLite 4,750x faster for single-host lookups (95ms → 0.02ms)
- Historical peak (202K records, 172MB): SQLite 29,806x faster (596ms → 0.02ms)
- At peak scale, monitor was unusable with JSONL - every status update took 600ms scanning all records
- SQLite maintains constant 0.02ms lookup time regardless of history depth

All four requested metrics measured:
- Read latency: 12.7x-29,806x faster depending on scale (single host), 1.3x-2.5x at bulk scale
- Write latency: 2.1x faster for batches (8.5x slower for single writes, acceptable tradeoff)
- Startup time: 5.5x slower (negligible 1ms cost)
- Memory: 3.6x better efficiency for bulk reads

Results conclusively validate the migration decision - JSONL approach was causing severe performance degradation that would only worsen over time without manual intervention.

title: Extend maintain command to rotate notes.jsonl
description:
Add optional notes.jsonl rotation to the maintain command without changing the notes operators see.

Current behavior and correction to the original plan:
- Host notes and note-clear tombstones are append-only records, normally stored in data/notes.jsonl; resolve the actual location through default_notes_path().
- fleetroll/notes.py reads the supplied active file through iter_audit_records(). Neither reader automatically discovers archives. Simply adding notes.jsonl to maintain's rotation list would hide existing notes and history from current views.
- .gitattributes applies merge=union to data/*.jsonl. A timestamped archive named notes.jsonl.<timestamp> does not match that pattern. Do not assume archives inherit the merge policy or that rotation solves concurrent Git edits.

Acceptance criteria:
- Choose and document a rotation/replay design before implementing it: either replay archives with the active file or preserve equivalent state and history through another explicit mechanism.
- Preserve each host's visible note text and count across rotation. Replay note-clear tombstones in the correct order so cleared notes never reappear; retain accessible note history.
- Define deterministic ordering and duplicate handling across active and archived records, including repeated rotations and subsequent note-add/note-clear operations.
- Define Git tracking and merge behavior for both active and archive files. Handle or explicitly guard against concurrent appends and rotations; do not rely on an unmatched merge=union pattern.
- Reuse maintain's size threshold, force, and dry-run behavior where appropriate. Dry runs must not change files or visible notes.
- Add focused tests for visible notes and counts before/after rotation, clears before/after rotation, multiple rotations, duplicate/order handling, dry runs, and the chosen concurrency/merge behavior.
- Update operator documentation with archive discovery, retention, and recovery behavior.

Keep P4: growth is slow (roughly 2 MB for 10,000 records at 200 bytes each), making this maintenance hygiene rather than urgent work. No implementation is requested by this ticket review.

title: Host List Generator
description:
## Host List Generator

Generate and maintain structured host list files under `configs/host-lists/`.

### Design Doc
See design details in the conversation — full spec covers directory structure, file formats, and script behavior.

### Directory Structure

```
configs/host-lists/
  linux/
    all.list              # human-maintained
  mac/
    all.list              # generated from puppet YAML (all groups, deduped+sorted)
    gecko-t-osx-1500-m4.list         # generated per-group
    gecko-t-osx-1500-m4-staging.list
    ...  (one per group)
  windows/
    all.list              # human-maintained scaffold
  combined.list           # generated from linux/all.list + mac/all.list + windows/all.list
```

### Script: `tools/generate_host_lists.py`

**Usage:** `generate_host_lists.py [--inventory-path PATH] [--host-lists-dir PATH] [--dry-run] [mac|combine]`

**Key behaviors:**
- Commented-out YAML targets are skipped (PyYAML ignores comments natively)
- Dedup: host appearing in multiple groups gets one entry, under the first source section
- Idempotent: only rewrites the `# --- generated ---` block; content outside is preserved
- Dry-run mode: prints what would change without writing
- Inventory path: defaults to `~/git/ronin_puppet/inventory.d/`, overridable via `--inventory-path` or `FLEETROLL_INVENTORY_PATH`

### File Format Notes

- `mac/<group>.list`: fully generated, per-group with metadata header
- `mac/all.list`: generated from all puppet groups, with per-group section headers and host counts
- `linux/all.list`: human-maintained (metadata header only, no generated section)
- `windows/all.list`: empty scaffold with metadata header
- `combined.list`: generated from all three OS all-files, deduped+sorted with source section headers

### Implementation Notes

1. `parse_host_list()` stays unchanged — generated files are valid .list format
2. Generated section replacement: marker-based (`# --- generated` to `# --- end generated`)
3. `windows/all.list`: create empty scaffold so directory structure exists from day one
4. Generated files get checked in — diffs make fleet changes reviewable in git

title: host-audit doesn't log SSH auth failures
description:
host-audit doesn't write records for SSH auth failures ("Permission denied"). 

**Root cause:** In audit.py:288-293, rc==255 is treated as a "connection error" which triggers retry logic. After max retries, the result is returned (lines 337-348) WITHOUT calling process_audit_result(), so NO record is written to host_observations.jsonl.

**The bug:** "Permission denied" means SSH is UP (host reachable, port open, daemon responded) but authentication failed. This should be logged immediately, not retried.

**Policy (user-defined):**
- SSH port responds (auth fails, protocol errors) → Log immediately  
- Can't connect (timeout, refused, DNS failure) → Retry, don't log unless persistent

**Current behavior:**
- "Permission denied" has rc==255 → treated as connection error → retried → never logged
- Example: ms-080 has been scanned many times but has 0 records in observations log

**Fix:** In audit.py:288-293, remove "rc == 255" from is_connection_error check. Add specific pattern matching:
- Connection errors (retry): "Connection refused", "Connection timed out", "Could not resolve hostname"
- Auth/protocol errors (log): "Permission denied", etc. (anything else with rc != 0)

This ensures reachable hosts with auth issues are logged (so monitor shows actual state) while unreachable hosts don't spam the log.
close_reason:
Fixed is_connection_error classification to distinguish auth/protocol failures from connection errors. Removed

- `gwhc_state` from mvp-z4lh (worker process state at time of last audit)
- TC job recency / success rate from mvp-6eri
- `data` age (already tracked, measures SSH reachability)

The filter remains the right combination layer. This bead is about ensuring those signals are good enough that the filter is trustworthy, not about replacing it with a pre-computed verdict.

title: Improved puppet run tracking
description:
## Problem

Currently, the host-monitor APPLIED and HEALTHY columns try to infer whether puppet has applied the current state by:
1. Comparing puppet's last run time against override file mtime
2. Tracking override removal times via unset records or audit transitions

This approach is fragile and requires complex heuristics. We can't reliably determine:
- When an override was removed (if done before auditing started or manually)
- Whether puppet actually applied the current configuration
- What git SHA the host was converged at

## Solution

Have the puppet wrapper script write out a state file with the actual applied state. This gives us ground truth instead of inference.

## Puppet State File

Location: `/etc/puppet/last_run_metadata.json` (or similar)

Fields to include:
- `ts` - ISO timestamp when puppet ran
- `success` - true/false
- `exit_code` - actual exit code
- `git_repo` - repository URL
- `git_branch` - branch name  
- `git_sha` - commit SHA that was applied
- `override_sha` - SHA256 of override file applied (null if none)
- `vault_sha` - SHA256 of vault file used (null if none)
- `override_path` - path to override file
- `role` - puppet role applied
- `duration_s` - how long the run took

## Benefits

1. **APPLIED becomes simple:**
   - Override present: Y if puppet.override_sha == current_override_sha and success
   - Override absent: Y if puppet.override_sha == null and success

2. **New columns possible:**
   - PP_SHA - does puppet's git_sha match expected rollout SHA?
   - OVR_MATCH - does puppet's override_sha match current file?

3. **No heuristics needed:**
   - Direct comparison of "what puppet applied" vs "what's currently there"
   - No guessing about removal times or boot times

## Implementation Steps

1. Modify run-puppet.sh wrapper to write JSON state file after each run
2. Update audit script to read and include puppet state in observed data
3. Update host-monitor to use puppet state for APPLIED/HEALTHY logic
4. Add new columns (PP_SHA, etc.) as needed

## Related

This supersedes the complex removal-time tracking logic that was being developed.

---

## Implementation Summary

This epic has been completed. The implementation uses a reusable bash function library approach:

**Architecture**:
- **Reusable function library**: `references/puppet_state_functions.sh` - OS-agnostic state writing function
- **Reference implementations**: Linux (ERB template) and macOS puppet wrapper scripts
- **Deployment location**: Function library installed at `/etc/puppet/lib/puppet_state_functions.sh`
- **State file location**: `/etc/puppet/last_run_metadata.json` (both platforms)

**Key Decisions**:
1. **JSON format with schema versioning** - Enables future format evolution
2. **SHA-based APPLIED logic** - Direct comparison of `puppet_override_sha_applied` vs `current_override_sha256`
3. **Backward compatibility maintained** - Fleetroll falls back to legacy YAML parsing if JSON unavailable
4. **Never-fail guarantee** - State writing errors logged but never block puppet runs
5. **Atomic writes** - Temp file + rename pattern prevents corruption

**New Monitor Columns**:
- **PP_SHA** - 7-char git SHA that puppet applied (informational)
- **PP_LAST** - Uses `puppet_state_ts` with fallback to legacy field
- **APPLIED** - SHA comparison (primary) with timestamp heuristic fallback

**Documentation**:
- `references/README.md` - Deployment guide and integration instructions
- `docs/puppet-state-tracking.md` - Complete feature specification
- `docs/rollout-health-verification.md` - Updated with SHA-based approach
- `README.md` - Added Puppet State File section

**Testing**:
- Unit tests added for state writing, parsing, and monitor logic
- Reference scripts include test and verification tools

All child tasks (mvp-uvz, mvp-14e, mvp-2us, mvp-13x, mvp-ahw, mvp-2xt, mvp-36e) completed.

title: host-unset-override: remove override from a population of hosts
description:
When a test branch is merged, remove its deployed override from a population selected using Fleetroll's shared monitor query engine, without maintaining temporary host lists.

This bead owns the shared population-removal foundation. Each supported host has one active override at its platform-specific path; selection identifies hosts and the exact deployed override content expected to be removed, not multiple simultaneous override files on one host.

Acceptance criteria:
- Add filter-based population selection using fleetroll/commands/monitor/query.py, preserving existing explicit host and host-list targeting.
- Use supported query syntax (for example ovr_bch~project-branch-name); do not introduce the obsolete override:branch syntax. Document that substring matching can select several branches and make the exact selected hosts and overrides reviewable.
- Reuse the existing unset command's default preview and explicit --confirm execution model. Do not introduce parallel --yes/--dry-run conventions without a separate CLI decision.
- Preview exact hostnames, expected override identities, source observation timestamps, and stale, missing, or failed evidence. A preview must not change managed hosts.
- Define selection freshness and execution-time verification. Before removal, verify the active override still matches the reviewed expected content; refuse changed or unknown content rather than deleting a replacement override.
- Reuse platform paths, per-host removal, audit logging, automatic observation refresh, and meaningful exit statuses. Treat already-absent overrides as idempotent no-ops.
- Provide per-host results and machine-readable output. Distinguish removal written from subsequent Puppet convergence.
- Test shared query behavior, explicit targeting compatibility, empty populations, preview/confirmation, changed overrides between selection and execution, partial failures, audit records, and refresh behavior.

mvp-t8yk depends on this foundation and adds source-commit selection. Keep population resolution, preview, verification, execution, and reporting shared; this bead does not define commit provenance semantics.

title: host-set-override: target a percentage of hosts by role
description:
Allow an operator to set a supplied override on a target percentage of the hosts with a specified Puppet role, without manually querying observations, calculating counts, selecting hosts, and maintaining temporary host lists.

Motivated by the legacy TC/perf sudoers rollout: expand Ubuntu 24.04 Talos from about 10% to 50% while retaining existing canaries and controls, and expand netperf from 50% to 100%.

Acceptance criteria:
- Accept a role, target percentage, and override file through the CLI; preserve existing explicit host/file targeting. Choose and document the option names during implementation.
- Interpret the percentage as total coverage of the role population, not an additional percentage per invocation. Count hosts already on the exact requested override SHA toward the target and retain them when expanding. Repeating the same target must not select another wave.
- Define and expose the population source, observation freshness, denominator, percentage validation, and rounding policy. Report stale, missing, unreachable, and otherwise ineligible hosts explicitly rather than silently shrinking the denominator.
- Select additions deterministically, preserve unselected hosts as controls, and retain existing protections against overwriting conflicting overrides. Report insufficient eligible hosts or a target already exceeded; lowering a percentage must not implicitly remove overrides.
- Preview the role population, current matching hosts, target count, additions, remaining controls, exclusions/conflicts, and exact selected hostnames. Explicit confirmation executes the reviewed selection, with relevant state changes detected before writing.
- Reuse the existing validated override deployment, audit logging, and observation refresh. Provide human-readable and JSON results, including per-host failures and achieved coverage. Keep override deployment distinct from verified Puppet convergence.
- Document examples for 10% to 50% expansion and 100% coverage. Test rounding and small/empty populations, invalid percentages, idempotent repeats, existing canaries, conflicting overrides, unavailable observations, partial failures, and preview/execution consistency.

Related: mvp-kq1h.2 covers filtered/limited host-run-puppet batches. Reuse selection concepts where practical without making Puppet execution a requirement for this feature. Parent mvp-3vc covers broader rollout orchestration.

title: Canary tool: summarize rollout and control results
description:
Add a concise results summary to the canary tool, scripts/check_override_jobs.py. Operators currently have to aggregate per-host rows and JSON manually to understand whether a rollout differs from its same-pool controls.

Acceptance criteria:
- Present an aggregate table for rollout and control cohorts, with host counts, task-run counts, completed, failed, exception, running, pending, and unknown outcomes. Support both worker-type comparison and explicit host-list reports.
- Show success/failure rates with documented denominators; do not count running, pending, unknown, or query errors as successful completed work. Distinguish failures from infrastructure exceptions and report the percentage-point difference between comparable cohorts.
- Show the comparison cutoff/window, override identity, observation freshness, requested versus successfully queried hosts, empty-task hosts, query errors, and the 20-task history/truncation limitation. Qualify summaries when coverage is incomplete or sample sizes are small.
- Summarize affected hosts and failure patterns by task/test name, distinguishing patterns observed in both cohorts from patterns seen only in the sampled rollout cohort. Keep task links and existing per-host detail available. Matching task names or aggregate rates alone must not imply matching root causes or prove a regression.
- Handle 100% rollouts with no remaining controls and host-only checks: provide useful standalone totals and explicitly mark the control comparison unavailable, rather than treating the absent cohort as successful or requiring controls for a summary.
- Add the aggregate summary to JSON output using a documented additive structure. Preserve existing per-host results and meaningful exit-status behavior for task failures and query errors; document behavior when controls are intentionally absent.
- Include examples and tests for mixed outcomes, partial query failures, truncated history, no tasks, no controls, multiple override groups, and rate-denominator edge cases.

Scope is presentation and aggregation of evidence the existing tool collects, without adding automatic rollout advancement, new historical storage, or claims of log-based failure classification. Related: mvp-xhk5 evaluates the checker and possible CLI integration; mvp-osyq covers rollout gating using Pool Classifier evidence. Coordinate any future integration with mvp-6eri.
close_reason: Implemented aggregate rollout summaries with outcomes, explicit rate denominators, attribution coverage/exclusions, failure patterns and links, standalone master/override reports, and versioned JSON. Validated with 52 focused tests, full suite of 1162 passing tests, pre-commit/type checks, and live master-canary smoke reports.

description:
Extend scripts/check_override_jobs.py into a general rollout report that compares the population within a Puppet role running master with the population running each distinct override. The same report should work during initial deployment, expansion, partial removal after merge, and full removal. Do not add a separate post-merge mode.

Motivation: after removing the legacy TC/perf sudoers override from ms-016 and ms-017, the current CLI refused to report their tasks because they no longer had an override SHA. A temporary script was needed to check jobs since successful convergence to merged master.

Acceptance criteria:
- Support role-based population selection and group its hosts into verified master/no-override and each distinct override configuration. Preserve relevant explicit host-list and worker-pool selection. Use observed Taskcluster worker identities where available; do not silently combine unrelated roles or pools.
- Compare every override cohort separately with the master cohort. Do not combine different overrides into one treatment group, and do not assume every no-override host has successfully applied master. Show actual applied revisions and distinguish differing revisions within a cohort when material.
- Attribute task runs using evidence of the configuration successfully applied when the run started. An override file written or removed is insufficient until Puppet convergence is verified. Include post-removal jobs, exclude jobs from the previous configuration, and report unknown or insufficient provenance explicitly.
- Use documented, comparable time windows and expose each cutoff and cohort membership. Determine configuration activation from deployment/removal events and successful convergence evidence; a routine later Puppet run must not silently move the activation cutoff. Where retained evidence cannot establish a transition, report that limitation rather than fabricate a timestamp.
- Reuse mvp-3vc.3 summary functionality: host and task counts, outcome totals, rates with explicit denominators, differences against master, task/test-name failure patterns, links, observation freshness, query failures, and recent-history truncation. Current configuration or task-name matches alone do not prove a failure cause or a regression.
- Produce useful standalone reports when only master or only override hosts remain; mark comparisons unavailable when a cohort is absent or has insufficient evidence. Support multiple simultaneous overrides, incomplete observations, and mixed convergence states in both human-readable and JSON output.
- Evaluate renaming the script/tool to a rollout-oriented name, such as check_rollout_jobs.py / rollout report. Record the choice, update documentation and help text, and retain a compatibility entry point or clear migration guidance for existing check_override_jobs.py users. Fleetroll CLI integration remains coordinated with mvp-xhk5.
- Test deployment and removal transitions, master-only and override-only populations, multiple overrides and applied revisions, jobs straddling a transition, ordinary repeated Puppet runs, missing audit/convergence history, query failures, and the 20-task coverage limit.

Related: mvp-3vc.3 owns aggregate results presentation; this bead owns population/configuration grouping, task attribution across transitions, comparisons, and naming. mvp-xhk5 evaluates Fleetroll integration. Preserve mvp-6eri / Pool Classifier responsibilities and avoid adding a competing historical task store or automatic rollout advancement (mvp-osyq).

title: Retain compact host configuration history for rollout reports
description:
Retain a compact, 30-day SQLite configuration timeline so rollout reports remain useful after the rolling ten full host observations are pruned. Follow-up to mvp-3vc.4; see docs/configuration-history.md for the constrained design and evidence contract.

Motivation: the first rollout report could attribute only one of 33 in-window tasks because the original convergence observations had already aged out. Saved snapshots restored useful coverage, but normal collection should preserve this evidence automatically. Measurements showed about 930 hosts and 1.4 KB per full observation: seven days of three-minute full scans would produce about 4.3 GB of raw JSON, mostly repeated state.

Acceptance criteria:
- Persist compact history atomically during normal observation collection before existing snapshot pruning, and incorporate relevant override/vault operation boundaries. Report execution remains read-only.
- Default to 30 days of compact history. Preserve the latest-ten full-observation policy and last successful observation exception; do not change unrelated table retention or the shared DB_RETENTION_LIMIT.
- Extend matching verified intervals on stable scans instead of appending full snapshots. Track material role, repository/revision, override/vault, worker identity, and verification-state changes. Repeated successful Puppet runs preserve the original configuration activation.
- Preserve explicit unknown intervals at failures, writes/removals before convergence, mismatches, conflicts, and unsupported observation gaps. Never bridge known uncertainty or extrapolate beyond observed evidence. Retain sufficient continuity metadata for the report's configurable gap policy; unsupported stricter queries fail closed.
- Store only allowlisted configuration metadata, hashes, observation/application bounds, and provenance. Keep enough override/master proof to survive ordinary cache/ref expiry without retaining secrets or command/file contents.
- Provide an additive idempotent migration, safe replay/concurrent writes, conservative late/conflicting-event behavior, 30-day expiry with cutoff-crossing anchors, and cleanup of unreferenced descriptors. Do not fabricate backfill for pruned evidence.
- Make rollout reports consume the timeline, deduplicate overlap with full/saved observations, and expose coverage, provenance, retention cutoff, and gaps. Keep saved snapshots usable.
- Test compact-versus-raw attribution equivalence for supported queries, stable polling, reruns, transitions/manual changes, failures/gaps, strict gap bounds, late/duplicate/conflicting evidence, role/revision/identity changes, reference expiry, retention boundaries, migration, and concurrent writers.
- Measure rows/bytes, indexes, collection/maintenance cost, and report latency on stable and changing/outage workloads for about 930 hosts. Stable polling must update bounded rows; storage scales with transitions/uncertainty rather than scan count. Document actual measurements instead of assuming a fixed MB estimate.

Non-goals: longer Taskcluster task retention, a new task-history store, automatic rollout decisions, or claiming detection of manual actions reverted between observations. Database schema, indexes, and descriptor deduplication are implementation choices within the documented evidence/retention contract.
close_reason: Implemented compact 30-day configuration history with atomic collection, conservative uncertainty and operation boundaries, migration and retention, read-only rollout reporting with provenance, comprehensive tests, and documented 930-host measurements. Full suite: 1204 passed; prek passed.

title: Improve monitor help with supported filter syntax and note examples
description:
Add a dedicated Filter Syntax section to monitor help, consistent with the shared query engine and docs/monitor-filter-sort.md.

Document the supported column/operator/value syntax, space-separated AND conditions, case-insensitive string comparisons, duration values, sort syntax, and supported field names/aliases. Reuse the existing reference documentation rather than inventing another query dialect.

Required note examples:
- note= selects hosts with no displayed note.
- note!= selects hosts with a displayed note.
- note~foo selects displayed notes containing foo.
- note!=foo excludes an exact displayed value of foo, not every note containing foo. It can include empty notes and strings such as foobar; displayed note counts are part of the compared value.

Remove the obsolete notes:\\!foo example. The current engine uses the singular note field and has no negated-substring operator. Do not imply that != negates contains or that arbitrary ! expressions are supported. Adding substring negation would be separate query-language work.

title: Integrate Pool Classifier workload evidence with Fleetroll
description:
Define and consume a versioned, read-only Pool Classifier integration for worker, pool, and rollout-cohort workload evidence.

Current behavior:
- Fleetroll's existing rollout report queries recent Taskcluster outcomes on demand and attributes them to verified configuration cohorts. It does not write a persistent task-history store.
- That report already computes sample-based totals, rates, and comparisons. It is not a Pool Classifier integration and must not be marked complete by this bead.
- Pool Classifier integration remains a proposal; no external summary API or compatibility contract is assumed to exist.

Ownership and scope:
- Pool Classifier owns shared outcome collection, failure classification, success-rate semantics, and collection coverage.
- Fleetroll owns host state, configuration/Puppet provenance, verified rollout cohorts, presentation, and operator actions.
- Reuse Fleetroll's collected worker identity and pool mapping, including historical identity and contradiction semantics where relevant. Define how physical hosts, TC workers, pools, cohorts, and report time windows map to Pool Classifier evidence.
- Agree a versioned read-only summary contract with the Pool Classifier producer before implementing a consumer. Specify outcome definitions, recency, sample size, coverage, categorized regressions, identity, and time-window/cohort scope.
- Add links from Fleetroll host/rollout views to corresponding Pool Classifier evidence where supported.
- Keep persistence limited to an explicit cache/presentation layer; do not add a competing raw task-history collector or store.

- Document which Pool Classifier evidence supplements or can replace each existing on-demand report calculation.
- Keep evidence sources, windows, attribution, and coverage explicit; never mix incompatible denominators or imply classified regressions from task-name groupings alone.
- Preserve the current report's behavior, JSON contract, exit semantics, and provenance limits unless an explicit migration is designed, documented, and tested. Do not remove its direct TC path as an incidental part of this ticket review.
- If the agreed integration replaces on-demand queries or rate calculations, define the migration/fallback behavior and avoid duplicate collection or competing definitions.

Acceptance criteria:
- Document the agreed producer/consumer contract and identity/cohort mapping, with representative fixtures.
- Test supported/unsupported versions, unavailable or stale summaries, mismatched worker/cohort/window scope, partial coverage, and insufficient samples.
- Missing or incompatible evidence remains unknown, never healthy and never automatic rollout approval.
- Document the effect on existing reports and downstream consumers mvp-2ip, mvp-osyq, and mvp-3jg8.
- Keep rollout gating, health-policy changes, and frozen-host presentation in their respective downstream beads.

title: Reduce code duplication between single and batch audit

def cmd_host_audit(args):

title: Add --hostname-only to host-monitor --once mode

- Only valid with `--once` (error if used without it)
- Mutually exclusive with `--json` (error if both specified)


title: Evaluate storage format for tc and host data (consider SQLite)
description:
Migrate host_observations and tc_workers from JSONL to SQLite.

## Decision
SQLite with hybrid schema: a few indexed columns + JSON blob for the full record. This preserves JSONL-like flexibility (new fields = just add to dict) while gaining indexed queries and eliminating full-file scans.

## Current Pain Points
- Monitor does O(n) scan of 49MB/58K-line host_observations.jsonl to find latest per host
- Same for tc_workers at 54MB/125K lines
- Unbounded file growth with manual rotation only
- No query capability beyond full scan

## Design

### Schema (host_observations)
```sql
CREATE TABLE host_observations (
    host TEXT NOT NULL,
    ts   TEXT NOT NULL,
    ok   INTEGER,
    data JSON NOT NULL,  -- full observation dict
    PRIMARY KEY (host, ts)
);
```

### Schema (tc_workers)
```sql
CREATE TABLE tc_workers (
    host TEXT NOT NULL,
    ts   TEXT NOT NULL,
    type TEXT NOT NULL,  -- 'worker' or 'scan'
    data JSON NOT NULL,
    PRIMARY KEY (host, ts)
);
```

### What stays the same
- audit.jsonl — stays JSONL (append-only, rarely queried)
- overrides/ and vault_yamls/ — stay as content-addressed files on disk

### Schema evolution strategy
- New fields: just add to the JSON dict (zero friction, same as JSONL today)
- Need to query a new field often: promote to a column via ALTER TABLE ADD COLUMN (no migration framework)
- json_extract() available for ad-hoc queries into the blob

### Migration path
- Read existing JSONL files, bulk insert into SQLite
- Keep old JSONL files as backups
- Use WAL mode for concurrent read performance

### What this unlocks
- O(log n) latest-record-per-host lookups via index
- Retention policy (keep latest N records per host, prune old)
- Ad-hoc queries (e.g. all hosts with failed puppet)
- Foundation for statistics panel (mvp-1ok) and other features
close_reason: Evaluation complete. Decision: SQLite with hybrid schema (indexed columns + JSON blob). See description for full design.

title: Investigate audit log truncation threshold
description:
Investigate when the audit log should be truncated to prevent performance issues.

## Analysis

The audit log is a JSONL file (append-only). Each record is ~500-1000 bytes containing timestamp, actor, action, host, SSH result, and observed state (role, override metadata, SHA256 hash).

### Actual Growth Rates (Observed)
- audit.jsonl: 94 MB in <1 week (~13 MB/day, ~4.7 GB/year)
- taskcluster_workers.jsonl: 37 MB in <1 week (~5 MB/day, ~1.8 GB/year)
- Much faster than initial estimates due to high operation frequency

### Performance Thresholds
- <100 MB: No concern
- 100 MB - 1 GB: Fine for append-only writes, full scans get slower
- 1 GB+: Should consider rotation/truncation
- 10 GB+: Definitely needs attention

## Implementation (2026-01-28)

### Decisions Made
1. **Split logs into three files:**
   - `audit.jsonl` - Real user actions only (set/unset override, set vault) - low velocity
   - `host_observations.jsonl` - Host state snapshots (host.audit) - high velocity
   - `taskcluster_workers.jsonl` - TC worker scan data (unchanged)

2. **Threshold: 100 MB** - Warn when any log file reaches 100 MB

3. **Manual rotation only** - No auto-rotation (user might be mid-operation)
   - Command: `fleetroll rotate-logs --confirm`
   - Only rotates files >= 100 MB threshold
   - Archives with timestamp: `logfile.jsonl.YYYYMMDD-HHMMSS`
   - New files start empty (no backfill)

4. **Warning in monitor** - Top header shows warning in yellow when logs exceed threshold
   - Format: "⚠ Large logs: obs=142M tc=156M (run 'fleetroll rotate-logs')"

### Rationale
- Splitting logs separates high-velocity observations from critical audit events
- 100 MB gives advance warning before performance degrades
- Manual rotation gives user control over timing
- No backfill keeps implementation simple and logs pure append-only

### Backward Compatibility
- Monitor reads from `host_observations.jsonl` if it exists, falls back to `audit.jsonl` for old data
- Graceful migration - no manual intervention needed
close_reason: Completed: Investigated log growth, implemented 3-way log split (audit/observations/TC), added 100 MB threshold with monitor warnings, and manual rotation command with --force flag. All tests passing.

title: Expose last successful worker identity for unreachable-host recovery
description:
Expose the last successfully collected worker identity as explicitly historical evidence in host monitor JSON, so Moonshot Medic can investigate an SSH-unreachable host without requiring that hung host to refresh its audit first.

Context and scope

Follow-up to mvp-khj3. Monitor JSON version 2 preserves the latest audit status and marks observed_worker_identity unresolved when the latest audit fails. Preserve those current-evidence semantics. Supply historical evidence and an explicit TC lookup path; Medic's reset policy, inactivity thresholds, and maximum acceptable baseline age remain outside this task. No reset action or reset authorization is added.

Implementation decisions agreed with the user

1. Baseline selection and retention

- Select the newest successful host audit with tc_worker_identity_status=ok and all four valid, nonempty string identity fields: provisioner, worker type, worker group, worker ID. Never fill missing fields from the role, override intent, or TC observations.
- Search past newer failed audits and successful audits with unusable identity collection. For example, Monday's complete identity remains the baseline after Tuesday's identity collection failure and Wednesday's SSH failure; the newer evidence is reported separately.
- Preserve one latest valid baseline per host until replaced by a newer valid identity collection, including a newer collection of the same identity. Do not automatically expire it. Repeated failures, newer incomplete successful audits, raw-observation pruning, and compact-history expiry must not erase the retained baseline or its source context.
- Reuse retained history to initialize the baseline where available. Missing recoverable history is explicit; never synthesize evidence. Current latest_ok alone is insufficient: it selects audit success, not identity collection success, and existing raw retention can prune an older usable identity.
- Keep the baseline's original observation timestamp, collection status/source, override SHA/presence, configured-pool context, and application status. JSON generation, failed audits, and TC lookup must never advance that timestamp. Expose freshness using the existing source-age convention; it is not a recovery age limit.

2. Newer evidence and override rules

Keep the historical baseline visible when uncertain or contradicted. Report contradiction status as none_known, uncertain, or contradicted, with machine-readable reason codes and supporting evidence timestamps. none_known means no known contradiction, not confirmed current identity or permission to reset. Preserve applicable reasons; a known contradiction takes precedence over uncertainty in the summary status.

| Newer evidence | Required treatment |
| --- | --- |
| Failed SSH audit alone | Preserve baseline; adds no contradiction or identity uncertainty by itself. Existing signals remain. |
| Identity collection error, parsing/invalid collection result, incomplete identity, or legacy audit without collection metadata | Preserve baseline and mark uncertain. A parser/collector failure does not prove the configured identity changed. |
| Explicitly missing worker configuration | Preserve baseline and mark contradicted. Distinguish this from inability to read/parse configuration. |
| Known override set/unset after baseline collection | Preserve baseline and mark contradicted, including writes recorded by Fleetroll without a successful subsequent SSH audit. |
| Unavailable override metadata or unknown intent/application evidence | Mark uncertain where no stronger contradiction is established; do not clear a known override-change block. |
| New complete, successfully collected identity | Replace baseline, including changes to provisioner, pool, group, or worker ID. Retain any outstanding override-change block as described below. |

A known override-change block clears only after a later successful audit satisfies all three conditions: (1) collects a complete valid worker identity, (2) confirms the resulting override state is applied using the existing override-convergence semantics, and (3) the collected identity's provisioner and worker type match the resolved effective configured destination. For override set, use the effective configured destination with the override applied; for unset, use the role-default provisioner/pool. Puppet success and matching deployed/applied override SHAs alone do not establish this destination match. A mismatched or unresolved destination keeps contradiction_status=contradicted and the override-change block in place, even when application_status=applied and the complete identity replaces the displayed historical baseline. Pending, failed, or unknown application remains blocked even if a new identity is collected and becomes the displayed baseline. A fresh matching TC lookup never clears that block. Source context must make pending/failed/unknown application visible rather than imply the identity is applied. Later failed SSH audits must not erase earlier contradictions. Retain the outstanding block with the baseline so history pruning cannot silently clear it.

3. Explicit historical TC lookup

- Add the opt-in interface `fleetroll gather tc --use-historical-identity HOST_OR_FILE`. Normal gather tc behavior is unchanged, including refusal to resolve a failed latest audit by silently using old identity or role/default pool.
- With this option, query the selected baseline's exact four-part identity for each host. Missing baselines fail explicitly with identity_unresolved and no role/default/short-ID fallback. Support the existing host-list and partial-batch behavior.
- Permit diagnostic lookups for uncertain or contradicted baselines. Preserve all warnings/signals; a successful query establishes fresh TC evidence about that identity, not baseline validity or reset authorization.
- Pin the baseline used for each lookup. Persist resolution_source=historical_worker_identity, its original source timestamp, full identity, and source override/application context on the attempt. If the baseline changes during the query, the result must still name the baseline actually queried, not be relabeled as validating its replacement.
- Keep the latest completed attempt separate from retained successful TC observations. Preserve existing distinct outcomes: success, identity_unresolved, pool_query_failed, worker_missing, worker_ambiguous, and task_lookup_failed. A failed or missing-worker lookup is never evidence of inactivity and never refreshes retained-success timestamps.
- Successful lookup must match all four identity fields and link to its produced successful observation using successful_observation_ts. Preserve that baseline provenance on the produced successful evidence as well. Default lookups and historical lookups use the existing latest-attempt semantics; neither invents a successful attempt from retained evidence.

4. Monitor JSON version 3

- Set worker_evidence_schema_version=3. Add historical_worker_identity; preserve the latest raw audit and meanings of configured_worker_type, observed_worker_identity, and existing taskcluster fields.
- The new object has explicit present/missing status; provisioner, worker_type, worker_group, worker_id; original observation_ts and freshness; collection status/source; source override/application context; and contradiction status, reason codes, and evidence timestamps. Missing baselines have null identity/source timestamps and explicit unknown contradiction assessment rather than a claim of none_known.
- Add separate full-identity historical_identity_match values (match/mismatch/unknown) for retained TC evidence and latest lookup attempts. These do not replace the existing current-identity comparisons. Equality of identity is distinct from matching the exact baseline provenance of a historical lookup.
- Expose the pinned historical baseline provenance on historical attempts and produced successful evidence, allowing consumers to detect baseline replacement. Keep original collection, attempt, successful-observation, and activity timestamps distinct.
- Snapshot JSON, initial follow JSON, and subsequent follow updates share this contract. Follow mode must reflect baseline, contradiction, override, TC-attempt, and freshness changes. Preserve existing outer framing.
- Document exact nested fields and fixed reason-code vocabulary, examples, and migration from version 2. Consumers must accept version 3 before using historical lookup evidence. None of these fields is a reset authorization verdict.

Acceptance criteria

1. Failed latest SSH audit remains unresolved in current evidence while a complete historical identity retains its original timestamp and source context.
2. Baseline selection searches past unusable newer audits. Missing/legacy/incomplete/failed collections are never promoted. Retention tests prove the baseline survives repeated failures, newer identity-less successful audits, and ordinary history pruning until replaced.
3. Test every row of the newer-evidence table, identity changes across all four fields, and persistence of contradictions across later failed audits and pruning. Collection/parsing failure is uncertainty; explicitly missing configuration is contradiction.
4. Test override set/unset after collection, including a recorded write with no subsequent successful audit. New valid identity alone does not clear a known override block; clearing requires later complete collection, confirmed application, and a resolved matching intended provisioner/pool. Regression: after set to a new pool, Puppet succeeds and override SHAs match, but the complete identity still names the old pool; baseline may update while contradiction_status remains contradicted. Clear only after a later successful complete collection both matches the intended destination and confirms application. Cover equivalent unset-to-role-default transitions, provisioner mismatch, and unresolved destinations. Pending, failed, unknown, and unavailable metadata remain explicit.
5. Historical lookup can produce fresh matching evidence while latest SSH audit fails. Missing baseline, failed pool query, missing/ambiguous worker, failed task lookup, and success remain distinct. Uncertain/contradicted diagnostic lookup success does not clear signals. Default gather tc behavior is unchanged.
6. Test an intervening baseline replacement during lookup: stored result retains the queried identity, source timestamp, and context; consumers can detect it does not validate the replacement baseline. Retained success and latest failure remain independently timestamped, and success links to the observation it produced.
7. Older base-pool TC evidence is never attributed to a newer override pool. Full-identity matching includes group and worker ID, and historical provenance matching is separate from current-evidence matching.
8. Version 3 snapshot/follow contract tests cover missing evidence, source timestamps/freshness, override/identity transitions, contradiction changes, and TC-only updates. Document version-2 migration and safe consumption without implementing Medic policy.

This session updates task decisions only; implementation has not been requested. Keep the bead open.

Clearing requires later complete collection, confirmed application, destination provisioner/pool matching, and observation of the recorded target override state. title: Replace die() with proper exception handling
description:

class UserError(FleetRollError):

raise UserError("Refusing to set override without --confirm")

except UserError as e:
    print(f"ERROR: {e}", file=sys.stderr)
    sys.exit(2)

This allows tests to catch exceptions and verify error conditions.

title: Document release notes publication workflow
description:
Document the release notes publication workflow in AGENTS.md or docs/.

## Background
The release notes generator uses version eras — each version's notes cover commits while that version was active. The current (unreleased) version is always labeled IN_PROGRESS.

## Workflow to document
1. Bump version in pyproject.toml to the next version (e.g. 0.2.3 → 0.2.4)
2. Generate notes for the now-finalized version: `uv run release-notes --version 0.2.3`
3. Review the generated file in `docs/release-notes/generated/`
4. Remove the orphans and git log sections if not needed for publication
5. Save the reviewed file one directory up to `docs/release-notes/`

## Success criteria
- Workflow is documented in a discoverable location (AGENTS.md or docs/)
- Version bump requirement (to finalize an era) is clearly explained
- Output directory convention (generated/ vs parent) is explained

Covers committed version-bump boundaries replacing legacy eras, generated versus reviewed notes, full checks, annotated tags at the notes commit, pushing upstream, publishing with --verify-tag and --notes-file, and verifying the release. title: Add trap cleanup to remote shell scripts
description:
The remote scripts use 'set -eu' but intermediate failures leave unclear state. In ssh.py remote_set_script (lines 148-171):

```shell
sudo -n chmod $m "$tmp"   # If this fails...
sudo -n chown $og "$tmp"  # ...this never runs, temp file orphaned
sudo -n mv -f "$tmp" "$op" # ...and this never runs
```

If chmod succeeds but chown fails, a temp file is left orphaned on the remote host.

Solution: Add explicit trap for cleanup:
```shell
trap 'sudo -n rm -f "$tmp" 2>/dev/null' EXIT
```

Apply to all remote script generators in ssh.py.

rollout-report: scope historical evidence to selected role or pool
description:
Role/pool-selected rollout reports currently include historical configurations outside the requested population. For example, `rollout-report --role gecko_t_linux_2404_talos_wayland` shows an old `gecko_t_linux_talos / releng-hardware / gecko-t-linux-talos-1804 / mdc1` master cohort with zero current hosts and zero classified tasks, adding irrelevant insufficient-sample health and unavailable-comparison entries.

Cause: `select_hosts()` selects hosts by latest recorded role/identity, but `summarize()` creates cohorts from all historical configuration intervals for those hosts. Apply report selection to historical evidence as well as host selection.

Agreed behavior:
- With `--role`, assess tasks only while their verified historical configuration belongs to that role. Preserve distinct pools within the requested role.
- With `--worker-type`, assess tasks only in that provisioner/pool.
- Explicit host lists retain history across roles and pools.
- Omit out-of-scope historical cohorts from health, comparisons, and report-wide evidence-limit calculations, including empty historical cohorts.
- Keep a compact note about omitted historical work and preserve investigative evidence in verbose/JSON output.
- Distinguish known out-of-scope work from unknown configuration evidence; do not let known other-role/pool work reduce in-scope attribution coverage. Unknown evidence must remain explicit and must not count as passes.

Acceptance criteria:
- Regression tests cover a host migrating from 1804 to 2404 Wayland: the role-selected report has no 1804 assessment/cohort/comparison entries, while valid 2404 evidence remains.
- Cover pool selection including provisioner, multiple pools within one selected role, historical task boundaries, empty historical cohorts, and unchanged cross-population history for explicit host lists.
- Verify summary counts, coverage denominators, evidence limits, human output, and JSON/details agree with the selection and preserve unknown evidence conservatively.
- Update `docs/rollout-report.md` and relevant CLI help to explain selection semantics.

Relevant implementation: `fleetroll/rollout_report.py` (`select_hosts`, `collect_host`, `summarize`, `compare_cohorts`, evidence assessment/rendering); tests in `tests/test_rollout_report.py`.
close_reason: Scoped verified historical intervals and tasks to the selected role or provisioner/pool before assessment. Preserved omitted evidence in JSON/details and separated known out-of-scope work from unknown coverage evidence; explicit host history remains unchanged. Added migration, empty-cohort, shared-window, coverage, failure-pattern, and rendering regressions; full suite passed (1263 tests), and prek passed.

title: host-set-override: support short hostname (FQDN) expansion
description:

  fleetroll host-set-override t-linux64-ms-239 --from-file ~/.fleetroll/overrides/ae5ca0e39500 --confirm

without needing to type the full FQDN.

Analogous expansion already works for host-list files via the `# fqdn: .suffix` directive in `parse_host_list`. The single-host path in `cmd_host_set` / `cmd_host_set_vault` bypasses that logic entirely.

Possible approaches:
- Add a `--fqdn-suffix` option to the command (explicit)
- Read a default suffix from config/env (e.g. FLEETROLL_FQDN_SUFFIX or ~/.fleetroll/config)
- Detect suffix from the host DB (look up the known FQDN for the short name)

Acceptance criteria:
- `fleetroll host-set-override t-linux64-ms-239 ...` resolves to correct FQDN before SSH
- Dry-run output shows the expanded FQDN
- Existing FQDN inputs (with dots) pass through unchanged

title: Add horizontal scrolling to host-monitor display
description:
Add horizontal scrolling capability to the host-monitor display to accommodate additional columns without losing data.

## Current Problem

The monitor currently drops columns when terminal width is too narrow:
- Drop order: vlt_sha → sha → role → ts → uptime → err
- This hides important information on narrow terminals

## Proposed Solution

Add horizontal scrolling with left/right arrow keys:
- HOST column: Frozen on the left (always visible)
- Other columns: Scroll horizontally with ← → arrow keys
- Up/Down arrows: Continue to navigate rows (existing behavior)
- PgUp/PgDn/Home/End: Continue to work for vertical navigation

## Column Layout

[HOST (frozen)] | [scrollable: STAT | ERR | ROLE | OVR_SHA | VLT_SHA | UPTIME | LAST_OK | TC_QUAR | TC_LAST | TC_START | TC_RESV]

## Implementation Details

1. Track horizontal scroll offset (col_offset)
2. Always render HOST column at position 0
3. Render visible subset of remaining columns based on:
   - Available terminal width minus HOST column width
   - Current horizontal scroll offset
4. Add key handlers:
   - KEY_LEFT: Decrease col_offset (if > 0)
   - KEY_RIGHT: Increase col_offset (if more columns exist)
5. Show scroll indicator in footer:
   - "← Columns 2-6 of 11 →" (when scrolled)
   - Or visual indicator like "◀ ▶" when more columns available

## Benefits

- No data loss on narrow terminals
- Supports adding new columns (e.g., TaskCluster data) without layout constraints
- Better UX for users with narrow terminals or many columns

## Testing Considerations

- Test with various terminal widths (80, 120, 160 columns)
- Test with long hostnames that exceed HOST column width
- Verify frozen column behavior
- Test edge cases (scroll to beginning/end)
close_reason: done

title: rollout-report: simplify default output and fix terminal rendering
description:
The rollout-report default output has become long and repetitive: assessment, cohorts, comparisons, coverage, and observed outcomes restate the same evidence. Repeated population identifiers, zero counters, and metadata make it difficult to see cohort health, whether comparison is possible, and what evidence is missing. User examples also show drifting indentation and joined lines; investigate terminal newline/cursor state as a separate rendering defect rather than assuming layout changes alone will fix it.

Agreed direction:
- Default output answers three questions: how are the cohorts doing, can we compare them yet, and how much evidence is missing?
- Compact header shows selected population, report window, host count, and approximate whole-pool pending tasks with freshness available.
- Combine cohort assessment and cohort breakdown into one table per population: cohort, current verified hosts, completed, failed, exceptions. State sample sufficiency and mixed applied revisions once near that table; retain unknown outcomes prominently when present.
- Present each comparison once, with its conclusion, shared time window, finished tasks per side against the minimum, and attribution coverage. Keep full-report cohort health distinct from shared-window comparison evidence.
- Print role/pool/group context once per population. Support multiple populations and long cohort names without ambiguity.
- Keep evidence limitations prominent: classified/retrieved runs, excluded outcomes including failures/exceptions/unknowns, query coverage/errors, observation freshness, and retrieval truncation. Phrase clean samples as no failures in verified tasks; do not imply unattributed work passed or automatically approve rollout.
- Move revision distributions, override SHAs, retention cutoff/span counts, detailed outcome breakdowns, and routine zero counters to --details/--verbose. Preserve meaningful warnings in default output.
- Replace the attribution progress bar with clear numeric coverage. Collapse duplicate caveats and warnings.
- Show override presence compactly when it adds information beyond verified cohort membership; do not conflate file presence with successful Puppet application.
- Preserve machine-readable evidence and existing JSON/exit-code semantics; this is a presentation rework.

Illustrative default structure: header/context; COHORT HEALTH table with full-window sample notes; COMPARISON with shared-window evidence; EVIDENCE LIMITS with excluded failures and collection limitations; hint for --details.

Acceptance criteria:
- Representative master/override report shows each cohort and comparison once, without repeated full population identifiers or redundant outcome/rate blocks.
- Cover insufficient sample, sufficient clean sample, observed failures/exceptions/unknowns, absent control, mixed revisions, multiple populations, query errors, low attribution, queue lookup failure, and unverified current configurations.
- Preserve explicit distinctions between full-window and shared-window counts, override presence and verified application, and known out-of-scope versus unknown evidence.
- All supporting diagnostics remain accessible via --details/--verbose and JSON; document the display hierarchy in docs/rollout-report.md and relevant help.
- Investigate/reproduce drifting indentation and joined output under a real PTY/tmux, including progress output and interaction with terminal state; add appropriate regression coverage for the verified cause. Check ordinary and narrow terminal widths and redirected/plain output.
- Verify the default report stays concise and readable with long role/pool/branch names and does not silently hide failures or evidence limits.

Related: mvp-csug tracks role/pool filtering of historical evidence (including unwanted old 1804 cohorts). Keep that selection/coverage change separate from this presentation work; account for its resulting scope semantics.

Relevant files: fleetroll/rollout_report.py, tests/test_rollout_report.py, docs/rollout-report.md. Before implementation, capture representative before/after output for review; create a design doc in docs/ if needed for the significant rendering rework.
design: See docs/rollout-report-display.md for the display hierarchy, symmetric comparison wording, population labels, and PTY newline strategy.
notes: User refinements: population headings use role: provisioner/pool; show worker group only with multiple regions. Comparison statements must identify higher rates on either cohort, without inferring deployment/removal direction. Preserve JSON compatibility.
close_reason: Replaced repeated report sections with per-population cohort tables, symmetric shared-window comparisons, and explicit evidence limits. Added role: provisioner/pool headings with groups only across multiple regions, wrapped long names, and retained supporting diagnostics in details/verbose without changing JSON or exit semantics. Reproduced LF-only drift under disabled ONLCR/OPOST and fixed TTY line endings without mutating terminal flags. Fixture shrank from 95 to 30 lines. All 1277 tests and prek passed; design in docs/rollout-report-display.md.

title: Harden gwhc evidence and add safe reboot mode
description: Follow up the operator-triggered best-effort reboot in mvp-h60g. Update gwhc in ronin_puppet to provide trustworthy, versioned task-state evidence, then add a safer Fleetroll reboot mode using worker quarantine and a fresh post-quarantine check. This work is required before any unattended or fleet-wide reboot policy. See docs/reboot-if-idle.md.
acceptance_criteria: gwhc represents unknown separately from IDLE and health status. Task evidence is authoritative from claim through final completion, fresh, and scoped to the current boot and worker instance; missing, stale, truncated, or inaccessible evidence is unknown. The versioned JSON contract includes state, evidence time and identity, and refusal reasons. Fleetroll rejects legacy or unsupported contracts. The safe reboot mode quarantines the actual Taskcluster worker, preserves longer existing quarantines, rechecks after quarantine using fresh evidence, and reboots only while quarantine remains effective. Fleetroll audits the decisions and distinguishes reboot requested from recovery. Recovery is reported only after a new boot and worker availability are verified. Tests cover races, unknown evidence, unsupported contracts, quarantine failure/expiry, and recovery failure.
notes: Scope boundary: mvp-6xh4 owns the upstream gwhc JSON schema version, documented compatibility/exit semantics, and Fleetroll diagnosis compatibility handling. This bead depends on that contract and owns the broader authoritative task-state evidence needed for reboot decisions, plus quarantine, fresh post-quarantine checks, reboot requests, and recovery verification. A schema version or zombie finding alone is insufficient proof of idleness. Preserve all existing freshness, boot/worker identity, race, and unknown-evidence acceptance criteria; extend the agreed contract where needed rather than creating a competing format.

title: Introduce Result dataclasses for command outputs
description:
Command functions currently return untyped dicts/tuples. Introduce typed dataclasses for better IDE support and self-documenting code.

## Current Pattern
```python
# Returns dict with implicit schema
result = {'host': h, 'ok': True, 'role': r, 'override_sha': sha}
```

## Proposed Pattern
```python
@dataclass(frozen=True)
class AuditResult:
    host: str
    success: bool
    role_present: bool
    override_present: bool
    override_sha: Optional[str] = None
    error: Optional[str] = None
    
@dataclass(frozen=True)
class SetResult:
    host: str
    success: bool
    previous_sha: Optional[str] = None
    new_sha: Optional[str] = None
    error: Optional[str] = None
```

## Result Types to Add
- AuditResult - for host-audit command
- SetResult - for host-set-override command
- UnsetResult - for host-unset-override command
- HostState - for monitor (may already exist partially)

## Benefits
- IDE autocomplete and type checking
- Self-documenting return values
- Easier refactoring (rename detection)
- Immutable by default (frozen=True)

## Location
New file: `fleetroll/results.py` or inline in each command module
close_reason: TypedDict or return type hints provide sufficient type checking without adding dataclass overhead. Can recreate if genuine pain emerges.

title: Monitor: SHA cache never refreshed (stale branch/symlink names)

- Call poll_sha_cache() in main loop in entry.py

Files affected:

- fleetroll/commands/monitor/entry.py (call poll_sha_cache in main loop)

title: Add --debug flag to release-notes for range verification
description:
Add `--debug` flag to `release-notes` CLI that prints an annotated `git log --oneline` output showing where each version boundary falls, making it easy to verify that version ranges are correct and no commits are misattributed.

When `--debug` is passed, the tool:

- Maps each commit SHA to its version range

title: host-reboot-if-idle: operator-triggered best-effort reboot
description: Implement the initial operator-triggered `host-reboot-if-idle` command for one Linux generic-worker host at a time. Run live `sudo gwhc --json` and request reboot only when the command succeeds and its valid JSON object has top-level `state` exactly equal to `IDLE`. Do not use cached Fleetroll observations. Do not quarantine or recheck in this version. This intentionally accepts the race between the check and reboot and current gwhc false-idle risk; do not use for unattended or fleet-wide reboot policy. Report reboot requested only after the reboot request returns success; report an unknown outcome if SSH disconnects before the result is known. See `docs/reboot-if-idle.md` for behavior and acceptance cases. Safer gwhc and Fleetroll work is tracked separately.
acceptance_criteria: One host per invocation. Only live Linux hosts with gwhc can proceed. A successful `sudo gwhc --json` with valid top-level `state` exactly `IDLE` is the sole authorization condition. Missing or non-Linux host, absent gwhc, command or SSH failure, malformed JSON, missing state, or any other state refuses reboot. Issue one `sudo systemctl --no-block reboot` request immediately after the check. Clearly distinguish request success, request failure, and unknown outcome; never claim host recovery. Record the check and request outcome in the Fleetroll audit log. No quarantine, second check, or cached-state fallback.

Updated quick-version shape: implement an operator-triggered, best-effort reboot command for Linux generic-worker hosts with gwhc installed. Run live sudo gwhc --json; fail closed on missing gwhc, command failure, malformed/unsupported output, or anything other than explicit IDLE. If IDLE, request reboot immediately without quarantine or a second check. Report reboot requested, not recovered. This intentionally retains the race where a task can be claimed after the check and the current gwhc false-idle risk; do not use this path for unattended or fleet-wide reboot policy. Follow-up work: harden gwhc task-state evidence and unknown handling, then add Fleetroll quarantine, fresh recheck, and recovery verification for a safer mode.
Safer gwhc contract and quarantine/recheck implementation are tracked in follow-up bead mvp-fw8r.

title: Implement tc-fetch command for TaskCluster worker data collection
description:
Add a new command to fetch TaskCluster worker data for specified hosts.

## Command Interface

fleetroll tc-fetch <host-or-file>

Accepts single hostname or file with host list (like host-audit).

## Implementation Steps

1. Parse host list: Use existing host-or-file parsing logic
2. Find roles: For each host, find most recent audit record (any action) and extract role from observed.role
3. Map roles to workerTypes: Use hardcoded lookup table:
   ROLE_TO_TASKCLUSTER = {
       "gecko_t_linux_talos": ("releng-hardware", "gecko-t-linux-talos-1804"),
       "gecko_t_linux_2404_talos": ("releng-hardware", "gecko-t-linux-talos-2404"),
   }
4. Fetch GraphQL data: For each unique workerType, query TaskCluster GraphQL API:
   - URL: https://firefox-ci-tc.services.mozilla.com/graphql
   - Query: ViewWorkers operation
   - Batch by workerType to minimize API calls
5. Match workers to hosts: Strip FQDN from hostname (e.g., t-linux64-ms-016.test.releng.mdc1.mozilla.com → t-linux64-ms-016) and match against workerId
6. Store results: Write to .fleetroll/taskcluster_workers.jsonl

## GraphQL Query

Use the ViewWorkers query, simplified to fetch only needed fields:
- workerId
- state
- lastDateActive
- latestTask.run.started
- latestTask.run.resolved
- quarantineUntil

## JSONL Format

Two record types:

Worker record (one per matched host):
{
  "type": "worker",
  "ts": "2026-01-27T04:30:00Z",
  "host": "t-linux64-ms-280.test.releng.mdc1.mozilla.com",
  "worker_id": "t-linux64-ms-280",
  "provisioner": "releng-hardware",
  "worker_type": "gecko-t-linux-talos-2404",
  "state": "running",
  "last_date_active": "2026-01-27T04:25:00Z",
  "task_started": "2026-01-27T04:20:00Z",
  "task_resolved": "2026-01-27T04:24:00Z",
  "quarantine_until": null
}

Scan record (one per workerType checked):
{
  "type": "scan",
  "ts": "2026-01-27T04:30:00Z",
  "provisioner": "releng-hardware",
  "worker_type": "gecko-t-linux-talos-2404",
  "worker_count": 15,
  "requested_by_hosts": ["t-linux64-ms-280.test.releng.mdc1.mozilla.com"]
}

## Error Handling

- If host has no audit record: Display "-" (no data) in output
- If role not in lookup table: Warn user, skip that host
- Fetch all workerTypes even if some hosts might not be found in TC data

## Output

Show summary of fetched data:
Fetching TaskCluster data for 5 hosts...
Found roles: gecko_t_linux_talos (3 hosts), gecko_t_linux_2404_talos (2 hosts)
Querying workerType releng-hardware/gecko-t-linux-talos-1804... 3 workers found
Querying workerType releng-hardware/gecko-t-linux-talos-2404... 2 workers found
Wrote 5 worker records and 2 scan records to .fleetroll/taskcluster_workers.jsonl
close_reason: done

title: gather-tc: resolve worker pools from observed identity instead of a role whitelist
description:
New Puppet roles can silently stop Taskcluster collection because gather-tc requires ROLE_TO_TASKCLUSTER entries. Pool changes should not require a Fleetroll code release.

Reproduced 2026-11-03 with t-linux64-ms-001/002/003.test.releng.mdc1.mozilla.com after migration to role gecko_t_linux_2404_talos_wayland:

    uv run fleetroll gather-tc -v <host-list>
    WARNING: Role 'gecko_t_linux_2404_talos_wayland' not found in lookup table, skipping 3 host(s)
    No hosts with mappable roles found. Nothing to fetch.

The command exits 0. Last successful TC observations remain from 2026-10-30 (001 17:39 UTC, 002 21:24 UTC, 003 22:16 UTC), against the former gecko-t-linux-talos-1804 pool. Fresh host audits coexist with four-day-old TC_ACT and DATA TC ages; HEALTHY becomes N even though Puppet matches. Current task activity has not been independently verified.

Root cause: fleetroll/constants.py ROLE_TO_TASKCLUSTER and fleetroll/commands/gather_tc.py map_roles_to_worker_types/resolve_host_worker_types omit unknown roles unless WORKER_TYPE_OVERRIDE is present. Puppet role names are not a reliable general transformation to worker pool names (the existing Linux mappings already reorder components).

Proposed fix:
1. Extend gather-host to read only the effective worker identity fields from the host's generic-worker configuration: provisionerId, workerType, workerGroup and workerId. Confirm configuration paths and service launch overrides on each supported OS during implementation. Persist these fields in observed metadata; never collect credentials or the full config. Record missing/unreadable identity explicitly without failing unrelated host auditing.
2. Make gather-tc prefer this observed identity for pool selection and worker matching. WORKER_TYPE_OVERRIDE describes deployment intent and may not yet be applied; surface a mismatch with observed configuration instead of blindly replacing the observed identity. A config read establishes configured identity, not proof of a running worker; confirm presence through Taskcluster.
3. Retain existing role/override resolution only as a clearly identified compatibility fallback for older observations lacking identity. Newly observed pools and roles require no whitelist entry. Avoid guessing pool names from roles or reusing a previous pool after migration.
4. Report unresolved hosts and failed lookups as collection failures, including quiet mode and a nonzero exit status when any requested host cannot be collected. Preserve last successful data and its original timestamp; never refresh freshness on failure. Make the collection gap visible so historical activity is not mistaken for current evidence of inactivity (coordinate broader health semantics with mvp-d0kx).

Acceptance and regression coverage:
- An unknown role with observed worker identity collects successfully without modifying ROLE_TO_TASKCLUSTER, including this Wayland case.
- A host moving pools is queried in the newly observed pool, not the cached old pool.
- WorkerGroup/workerId matching handles identities that differ from the short hostname and avoids cross-group collisions.
- Older observations, absent/unreadable config, configured-versus-intended pool disagreement, missing workers, and partial API failures have explicit tested outcomes.
- Unresolved-only and mixed-success gathers report failures in verbose and quiet modes without advancing failed hosts' TC observation timestamps.
- Host collection output and logs never include worker credentials.

Scope: file the bug and proposal now; implementation remains open. Simply adding the Wayland role to the static table is insufficient.
notes:
Agreed implementation scope: gather effective worker identity on Linux and macOS; prefer it in gather-tc with legacy resolution only for older observations; explicitly report unresolved hosts and return nonzero; cover unknown roles, migrations, identity matching and fallback. Verify configuration paths and service launch overrides first. Defer monitor HEALTHY/display semantics to mvp-d0kx.
Implementation decisions documented in docs/worker-identity.md: parse identity remotely using Puppet Ruby; use running config arguments and managed launch paths, reject ambiguity and relative config paths; observed full identity wins over deployment intent; fallback only when older observations lack the status marker. Save partial successes, preserve failed timestamps, return nonzero. Live Linux Wayland and macOS R8/M4 identity collection verified.
Quiet-mode follow-up: moved per-host identity/fallback/mismatch diagnostics behind gather-tc -v. Quiet mode aggregates counts in one TC summary, marks failed collections FAILED, retains nonzero exit status and avoids duplicate CLI error output. Added bounded-output regression tests for 30 unresolved hosts, complete API failure, partial failures, fallbacks and pool mismatches.
Compact summary refinement: quiet TC output now shows only status, collected/requested counts, elapsed time and a short verbose hint, capped at 80 visible characters. Removed overlapping not-collected, unresolved, no-role and scan counts from the quiet summary; detailed diagnostics remain under -v.
close_reason: Implemented Linux/macOS worker identity collection from effective JSON/YAML config using Puppet Ruby, including managed launch configuration selection. gather-tc now queries observed pools and exact worker group/ID, warns on override intent disagreement, and limits legacy role fallback to older observations. Unresolved identities, missing workers and API failures return nonzero while preserving failed timestamps and committing partial successes. Documented decisions in docs/worker-identity.md. All 1103 tests and prek passed; live Linux Wayland hosts 001-003 and macOS R8/M4 identity checks passed.
